Title: Expand question pools for games with real headroom left
Category: AI

get-spec output:
Current pool sizes (backend/trivia/data/manifest.json): heatmap 6, tictactoe 8, bingo 10, connections 40, nba-grid 12, name-logo 30, fan-favorites 24, who-would-win 30 -- versus playoff-series 912, wordle 525, mvps 71, starting-five hundreds. series-winner (playoff series), guess-mvps, name-logo are already close to the ceiling of real NBA history (every real playoff series, every real MVP season, every real franchise logo) -- do not invent fictional ones to pad these. Double-check wordle specifically for room to add more eligible player names before concluding it is maxed out. For every other game -- heatmap, connections, nba-grid, bingo, career-path, who-are-ya, tictactoe, contexto, fan-favorites, pack-five, superdraft, imposter, who-would-win -- there is real room to grow. Fan out one independent sub-agent per game so each generation run correctness-checks against just that game. Follow each existing generator/validator under backend/trivia/games/ or backend/trivia/questions/games/ (materialize/validate/build_pool already exist per game) rather than inventing a new format. Hard requirement: every generated question must be verifiably correct against the real curated players dataset -- no hallucinated stats, teams, seasons or facts; run each game existing validator against anything generated and reject/regenerate on failure. Prefer content variety (eras, teams, criteria types) over near-duplicates. There is no content-quality style guide yet for question generation -- if solid, reusable guidelines emerge, note them for a future task. Note: heatmap, connections, nba-grid, bingo, pack-five, superdraft and imposter are currently hidden from players in the live app (see hidden flag in src/utils/GameUtils.tsx) -- keep maintaining/expanding their data anyway, hidden is not deleted.

6	## 2026-08-29 — Native plan-and-self-review step for hard-task design rounds, not superpowers:writing-plans
7	Context: asked to have planner-architect use the `superpowers:brainstorming`/`writing-plans`
8	skills for complex tasks (write a plan, self-review it, hand it to the engine).
9	Decision: build the same rigor (numbered plan, self-review for coverage/placeholders/
10	consistency/scope/ambiguity) directly into `design-round`'s procedure instead of invoking those
11	skills. Two reasons: (1) `superpowers:brainstorming` hard-gates on human approval before any
12	implementation step — incompatible with an unattended pipeline run; (2) both skills are
13	machine-local plugins, not committed to this repo, so referencing them would silently no-op on
14	every cloud routine run (the pipeline's primary execution mode).
15	Consequences: the plan-and-self-review discipline now runs identically local or cloud, with no
16	external dependency. If those skills are ever made repo-portable and their approval gate made
17	optional for headless use, this can be revisited.

19	## 2026-09-06 — Model policy: cheap implementer, heavy planner and reviewer
20	Context: the owner wants token spend cut without losing quality. Previously `classify` sent
21	hard tasks to an opus or fable *engine*; sonnet/haiku only implemented easier tiers. Reviewer
22	and QA models were fixed by frontmatter/profile, so the `deep`/`max` profile could silently put
23	browser-qa on opus.
24	Decision: split the pick in two. `engineModel` is haiku (trivial) or sonnet (everything else,
25	hard included) — never opus/fable. `planModel` is opus (explicit spec) or fable (thin spec) and
26	drives the design round, the replan, and code-reviewer. Every design round now produces a
27	full implementation plan (previously hard-only), explicit enough that sonnet executes it
28	rather than reasoning it out. test-qa-engine and browser-qa are always sonnet; the CTO gate
29	is pinned to opus in the workflow (never fable). The orchestrator passes every model
30	explicitly. Revisits 2026-08-29: `superpowers:writing-plans` may be used for the plan when it
31	is present in the skill listing (local runs); the native a–c step remains the cloud fallback.
32	`superpowers:brainstorming` stays excluded — its human-approval gate is still incompatible
33	with unattended runs.
34	Consequences: opus/fable spend moves from implementation (the longest stage) to two short
35	stages (plan, review). Plan quality is now load-bearing for hard tasks — a thin plan will
36	show up as sonnet build failures and verify fix-cycles, which is the signal to fix the plan,
37	not to raise the engine model.

This task is **hard** and **high risk**, and it needs a design round before any building starts:

- **Hard:** it generates new question data for about 13 games. The rubric names "work that generates or regenerates data consumed by several games" as hard.
- **Areas:** backend and data, where the generators and validators live under `backend/trivia/games/` and `backend/trivia/questions/games/`, plus games. It needs no frontend change: the hidden flag in `GameUtils.tsx` stays as it is.
- **High risk:** it touches the data pipeline (building, validating and refreshing pools, then the manifest).
- **Opus implements:** high risk sends the engine to opus. Checking generated facts against the players dataset also takes judgment at every step.
- **Fable plans:** Fable runs the design round, as on every task.

This wasn't a close call, so I added nothing to `DECISIONS.md`. `RETRO.md` has no parked tasks yet.
